blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Corporate tax, in practice, is a year-long cycle rather than a single event. The return is filed once a year, but the inputs are built throughout the year: provisions are made at the end of each quarter, adjustments are posted at month-end, and deductions are captured the moment they are incurred, not months later.

A well-run corporate tax process looks calm in March, when many companies are panicking, because ninety per cent of the work has already been done by then. The team knows roughly what the final tax will be, has already set aside the cash, has already drafted the return, and is simply running final checks.

A badly run process looks the opposite. The team is suddenly hunting for supporting documents, reconciling accounts that should have been reconciled monthly, and negotiating extensions with the tax office. Neither version is glamorous. The calm one saves everyone's weekends; the panicked one steals them year after year.

items.q: According to the text, when is the corporate tax return actually filed?
options: Every month
At the end of each quarter
Once a year
Whenever a deduction is incurred
items.why: "The return is filed once a year" — embora os insumos sejam construídos ao longo do ano.

items.q: Why does a well-run process look calm in March?
options: Because corporate tax is not due until April
Because the tax office grants an automatic extension
Because about ninety per cent of the work is already done
Because the team hires temporary staff
items.why: "ninety per cent of the work has already been done by then."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Deductions should be captured when they are incurred.
Setting aside cash early helps the team stay calm.
Reconciling accounts monthly reduces stress later.
Corporate tax should be treated as a single event in March.
items.why: Inferência: todo o texto defende que imposto corporativo é um ciclo anual, não um evento único.

items.q: The phrase "the panicked one steals them year after year" suggests that…
options: the problem repeats because the process is never fixed
a badly run process is a one-off mistake
weekends are lost only during the first year
the tax office is responsible for the lost time
items.why: Inferência: "year after year" indica que o padrão se repete enquanto o processo não muda.

items.q: What can be inferred about the team that hunts for supporting documents in March?
options: They filed the return ahead of the deadline
They had already set aside the cash
They fell behind on work that should have been done earlier
They reconciled their accounts every month
items.why: Inferência: procurar documentos e reconciliar contas na última hora mostra trabalho deixado para trás.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie explicando como está reconstruindo o processo de imposto corporativo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, here's the goal I've set for the team. By the time the official deadline arrives, ninety per cent of the work should already be done, and the last ten per cent should be completely routine. No heroics, no lost weekends.

The way we get there is simple to say and hard to do: we stop treating tax as a March problem. Every month-end, we post the adjustments while the numbers are fresh. Every quarter, we make the provision and set aside the cash, so there are no surprises when the bill lands. And the moment a deduction is incurred, we capture the supporting document — not three months later, when nobody can find the invoice.

I've watched the panicked version too many times. People hunting for paperwork, reconciling accounts that should have been closed months ago, calling the tax office to beg for an extension. It's exhausting, and it steals the same weekends every single year.

If we do the boring monthly work properly, March becomes a checking exercise. That's the whole idea. Calm is not luck — it's the result of eleven quiet months.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What goal has Sophie set for the team?
options: To file the return a month before the deadline
To have ninety per cent of the work done by the deadline, with the rest routine
To cut the tax bill by ten per cent
To stop making quarterly provisions
items.why: "ninety per cent of the work should already be done, and the last ten per cent should be completely routine."

items.q: What does Sophie say the team does at every quarter?
options: They hunt for supporting documents
They file a partial return
They make the provision and set aside the cash
They renegotiate the deadline with the tax office
items.why: "Every quarter, we make the provision and set aside the cash."

items.q: According to Sophie, when should a supporting document be captured?
options: Three months after the invoice arrives
The moment the deduction is incurred
When the tax office requests it
Only at the year-end close
items.why: "the moment a deduction is incurred, we capture the supporting document — not three months later."

items.q: When Sophie says "Calm is not luck — it's the result of eleven quiet months", she implies that…
options: the team should take eleven months off
March is the only month that matters
the calm March depends on steady work done all year
luck plays the biggest role in a good tax cycle
items.why: Inferência: a tranquilidade em março é consequência do trabalho constante nos meses anteriores.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's attitude toward the 'panicked version'?
options: She rejects it as exhausting and preventable
She is indifferent to it
She thinks it only happens to small companies
She sees it as unavoidable
items.why: Inferência: ela chama o padrão de exaustivo e propõe o trabalho mensal como forma de evitá-lo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We make a provision at the end of each quarter for the tax we expect to owe." A provision is…
options: a document that supports a deduction
an amount set aside in the accounts for a future cost
a deadline extension
a final tax payment sent to the authorities
items.why: Provision = provisão: valor reservado nas contas para um custo futuro.

items.q: "The bookkeeper will post the adjustments at month-end." To post here means to…
options: send something by mail
record an entry in the accounts
publish a public notice
delay a payment
items.why: To post = lançar: registrar um lançamento na contabilidade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Every eligible expense is captured the moment it is ___, not months later."
options: incurred
reconciled
drafted
filed
items.why: To incur = incorrer: o custo passa a existir no momento em que é assumido.

items.q: "We asked the tax office for an extension." An extension is…
options: an additional deduction
extra time to meet a deadline
a formal audit
a reduction in the amount owed
items.why: Extension = prorrogação: prazo adicional para cumprir uma obrigação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Once the cash is ___ each quarter, the final bill brings no surprises."
options: filed
posted
set aside
incurred
items.why: To set aside = reservar: separar o dinheiro antecipadamente para pagar o imposto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem numa rotina de imposto corporativo. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the draft return before we file." To sign off on means to…
options: quietly ignore
formally approve
postpone indefinitely
rewrite from scratch
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We agreed the monthly close, but the team never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to completion
delegated it to auditors
documented it in detail
did it ahead of schedule
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's set aside the cash for the tax bill now." To set aside means to…
options: postpone the payment
report it to the board
spend it elsewhere
reserve it for a specific purpose
items.why: Set aside = reservar, separar recursos para um fim específico.

items.q: "Doing the boring monthly work is what makes March calm — it really moves the needle." This means it…
options: wastes valuable time
is impossible to measure
makes a noticeable difference
creates resistance in the team
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "When the numbers don't match, we have to reconcile the accounts." To reconcile means to…
options: file the return early
close the accounts permanently
approve a deduction
make two sets of figures agree
items.why: Reconcile = reconciliar/conciliar: fazer dois conjuntos de números baterem.
